extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors and peer reviewers of healthcare quality improvement (QI) reports / manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reporting systematic, data-driven healthcare quality, safety and value improvement studies (SQUIRE 2.0). Covers the items authors should include in manuscripts to ensure transparent, complete reporting and to enable appraisal and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate that the manuscript concerns an initiative to improve healthcare (broadly defined to include the quality, safety, effectiveness, patient-centredness, timeliness, cost, efficiency, and equity of healthcare, or access to it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the title descriptive and simple so readers immediately know the work is a healthcare improvement initiative; describe the aim of the project and the context. Use terms that facilitate indexing (improvement-related MeSH terms) and make it easy for readers to identify the report as healthcare improvement work. Examples provided (eg, ‘Reducing post-caesarean surgical wound infection rate: an improvement project…’).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate information to aid in searching and indexing and summarise all key information from various sections of the text using the abstract format of the intended publication or a structured summary such as: background, local problem, methods, interventions, results, conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both descriptive (purpose, methods, scope) and informative (results, conclusions, recommendations) elements; include keywords and phrases to aid retrieval; follow journal-specific format/length requirements; structured abstracts (background, local problem, methods, interventions, results, conclusions) are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem description
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and significance of the local problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify the local (or specific) quality gap by describing current practice versus achievable evidence-based standard, including magnitude and relevance. Provide local system/context information that shows how the problem affects quality, outcomes, costs or safety. If the work is regional/national, interpret 'local' as the specific problem scope for that study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of what is currently known about the problem, including relevant previous studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise relevant evidence and existing best practice; situate the project within existing literature to justify the need for the improvement work and to support sustainability and generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal or formal frameworks, models, concepts, and/or theories used to explain the problem, any reasons or assumptions that were used to develop the intervention(s), and reasons why the intervention(s) was expected to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit the theory, logic model, or programme theory that underpins why the intervention should work (can be formal theory or general framework). State hypotheses about mechanisms and variation; use frameworks (eg, FITT, COM-B, Behaviour Change Wheel, MRC guidance) where helpful; an explicit rationale enables evaluation of mechanisms and transferability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the project and of this report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State aims clearly, completely and precisely; align aims with the problem description and rationale. When appropriate, specify both process and outcome aims and measurable targets so readers can judge whether the intervention was adopted and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual elements considered important at outset of introducing the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe setting, location, patient population, size, staffing, practice type, prior QI experience and other contextual factors thought a priori to influence success. Explain selection criteria for sites/teams if multisite. Consider using published context frameworks (eg, MUSIQ, CFIR, PARiHS) and plan to measure contextual factors prospectively if they are hypothesised to moderate outcomes; report how context might limit generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the intervention(s) in sufficient detail that others could reproduce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the intervention content, delivery, timing, personnel and resources; specify the team involved and roles; provide timelines, sequence of steps, materials, training and implementation strategy; report modifications made during the project and reasons for them. Consider using TIDieR or similar checklists for detailed intervention description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of the intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach chosen for assessing the impact of the intervention(s) and the approach used to establish whether the observed outcomes were due to the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the study design and methods used to assess causal attribution (eg, time-series, controlled designs, mixed methods); describe how internal validity was addressed (controls for confounding, design choices) and how the study distinguished intervention effects from secular trends or other influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures chosen for studying processes and outcomes of the intervention(s), including rationale for choosing them, their operational definitions, and their validity and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define process, outcome and balancing measures; provide operational definitions and measurement procedures; report evidence for validity/reliability where available; describe methods for ongoing assessment of contextual elements, and methods to assess completeness and accuracy of data (data quality assurance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative and quantitative methods used to draw inferences from the data, including methods for understanding variation within the data and the effects of time as a variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify statistical and analytic techniques (eg, statistical process control, time-series, regression, qualitative approaches, integration strategies for mixed methods). Describe how variation and trends over time were analysed and how inference was drawn from combined qualitative and quantitative data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical aspects of implementing and studying the intervention(s) and how they were addressed, including, but not limited to, formal ethics review and potential conflict(s) of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe oversight (ethics board review or justification for QI classification), consent procedures (if applicable), confidentiality protections, management of conflicts of interest, and other ethical protections for participants and staff. Discuss ethical issues specific to QI vs research when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial steps of the intervention(s) and their evolution over time (eg, timeline diagram, flow chart or table), including modifications made to the intervention during the project; details of the process measures and outcomes; contextual elements that interacted with the intervention(s); observed associations between outcomes, interventions and relevant contextual elements; unintended consequences; details about missing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present sequence and timing of activities and adaptations, quantitative outcomes and process measures, qualitative findings about implementation and context, associations and plausible causal links, and any unexpected effects (benefits, problems, costs). Report data completeness and missingness and provide visualisations (run charts, SPC) where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Key findings, including relevance to the rationale and specific aims, and particular strengths of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise synthesis of main results in relation to aims and rationale; highlight major strengths such as robust design, fidelity of implementation, or rich contextual analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature of the association between the intervention(s) and the outcomes; comparison of results with findings from other publications; reasons for any differences between observed and anticipated outcomes, including the influence of context; costs and strategic trade-offs, including opportunity costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss mechanisms and plausibility of causal links, situate findings within existing literature, explore how contextual factors may have modified effects, and report resource implications and trade-offs that affect adoption and scale-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits to the generalisability of the work and factors that might have limited internal validity such as confounding, bias or imprecision in the design, methods, measurement or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about threats to validity (selection bias, confounding, measurement error, Hawthorne effect, missing data), how these were mitigated, and how they affect interpretation and applicability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Usefulness of the work, sustainability, potential for spread to other contexts, implications for practice and for further study in the field, and suggested next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the practical implications, discuss sustainability and scalability, recommend specific next steps for practice, policy or research, and indicate how the work contributes to cumulative knowledge about improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding that supported this work and the role, if any, of the funding organisation in the design, implementation, interpretation and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and explicitly state the funders' role (or lack thereof) in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation and manuscript preparation to allow assessment of potential influence.
